1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Vijay Singh Gour, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Sunil Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3.

Applicant seeks bail in Session Trial No.59 of 2020 arising out of Case Crime No.003 of 2020,
under Sections 498A and 302 I.P.C., Police Station Bela, District Auraiya, during the pendency of trial.
4. This is the third bail application on behalf of the applicant.

The first one was dismissed for want of prosecution and the second bail application was rejected by this Court vide order dated Vinod Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61444291/

sentences.text: "1. List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Vijay Singh Gour, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Arun Kumar Mishra, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as perused the record.
3.

This is the second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant in Sessions Trial No.59 of 2020 arising out of F.I.R./Case Crime No. 003 of 2020, under Sections 498-A, 302 of IPC, Police Station- Bela, District- Auraiya, with a prayer to enlarge him on bail.
The first one was rejected by this Court vide order dated 21.02.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.17540 of 2020.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.17540 of 2020
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 4. As per the prosecution story, the marriage of the daughter of the informant was solemnized with the applicant as per Hindu Rites in the year 2006.

Subsequent to it,
the applicant and his family members are stated to have subjected her to cruelty for a demand of Rs.50,000/- and a car as dowry, thereby leading to her death on 01.01.2020.
In the meantime, the daughter of the informant is stated to have given birth to three daughters.
It is also stated that the applicant and his family members have taken the dead body of the deceased to Primary Health Centre, Sahar and ran away.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the site plan indicates that the place where the dead body was kept in an open space and there is no possibility of the applicant and his family members of murdering her.
The cause of death has been found to be asphyxia due to strangulation.
Learned counsel has further stated that the offence was committed elsewhere and not within the house of the applicant.
The victim was psycho patient and was undergoing treatment from 05.01.2007 to 18.12.2019 and was also under continuous stress.
Learned counsel has further stated that the medical report indicates that the victim had earlier on attempted to commit suicide and had even eaten rat repellent.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant has also stated that the applicant has no criminal history and has to look after his three daughters who have been left to lead a life of destitution and vagrancy.
The grand-father and grand-mother are looking after them.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 05.01.2020.
The period of incarceration is itself a ground for bail as his fundamental right enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution of India stands violated.
Learned counsel has next contended that to date only one prosecution witness i.e. the informant has been examined and that too on 18.03.2020.
The trial is proceeding at a snail's pace.

7. Per contra, learned AGA has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail on the ground that cause of death has been found to be asphyxia due to throttling and not by hanging, as such, the said death cannot be termed as suicide.

The only way the Vinod Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61444291/
2 deceased had expired is by homicide, as such, the provision of Section 106 of IPC stand attracted as the applicant has to explain as to how the death of the deceased has occurred withing the precincts of his house.
8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties, this Court is of the view that the deceased had expired within the precincts of the house of the applicant and that too by throttling, I do not find it a fit case to enlarge the applicant on bail.
9. In view of the above, the present anticipatory bail application is rejected.

10. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously, in view of the principle laid down in the recent judgements of the Apex Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial."
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that as a new ground, the applicant is incarcerated for about five years as he is in jail since 05.01.2020.
Only four witnesses have been examined and there is no likelihood of early conclusion of trial in near future.

Learned counsel has further stated that the cause of death was found to be asphyxia as a result of strangulation, but the said strangulation can be caused by the victim herself as she was a psychiatric patient as is but evident from the document.
She was undergoing treatment since 2006 and as such she was suffering from mood disorders.
The Fundamental Rights of the applicant enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution of India stand violated.
There is no criminal history of the applicant and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
6. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application.
7. A report was called from the Trial Court, whereby it is stated in the report dated 13.12.2024 that four witnesses have been examined.

Two witnesses are of fact and two are the formal witnesses and another witness is to be examined subsequently.
8.

The said report categorically states that no adjournment has been moved on behalf of the applicant to adjourn the case when the witnesses were present in court, as such, the delay cannot be attributed to the applicant.
The delay, if any, may be attributed to the prosecution.

9. ?The Supreme Court while granting bail to former Tamil Nadu Minister in V. Senthil Balaji v.
Enforcement Directorate, 2024 SCC OnLine SC 2626 held that higher thresholds for granting bail in stringent penal statutes like the PMLA, UAPA, and NDPS Act cannot be a tool to keep an accused Vinod Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61444291/
3 incarcerated without trial.

Enforcement Directorate, 2024 SCC OnLine SC 2626
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It emphasized the incompatibility of stringent bail provisions with prolonged delays in trial.

10. While granting bail to ex-West Bengal Minister in Partha Chatterjee v. Enforcement Directorate,
2024 SCC OnLine SC 3729, the Supreme Court reiterated the principle that "a suspect cannot be held in custody indefinitely and that undertrial incarceration should not amount to punitive detention."

entities.text:
Partha Chatterjee v. Enforcement Directorate,
2024 SCC OnLine SC 3729
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
"The Court would, nevertheless, ensure that affluent or influential accused do not obstruct the ongoing investigation, tamper with evidence, or influence witnesses,
namely, actions that undermine the fundamental doctrine of a fair trial," observed the bench.

11. The Supreme Court in the case of Union of India vs. K.A. Najeeb, AIR 2021 SC 712, has observed as under:-
"We are conscious of the fact that the charges levelled against the respondent are grave and a serious threat to societal harmony.

entities.text: Union of India vs. K.A. Najeeb, AIR 2021 SC 712
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Had it been a case at the threshold,
we would have outrightly turned down the respondent's prayer.

However, keeping in mind the length of the period spent by him in custody and the unlikelihood of the trial being completed anytime soon, the High Court appears to have been left with no other option except to grant bail."

12. The Supreme Court in the case of Niranjan Singh and another vs. Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and Others, AIR 1980 SC 785 has avoided detailed examination of the evidence and elaborate documentation of the merits of the case as no party should have the impression that his case has been prejudiced.

entities.text: Niranjan Singh and another vs. Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and Others, AIR 1980 SC 785
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A prima facie satisfaction of case is needed but it is not the same as an exhaustive exploration of the merits in the order itself.

13. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and taking into consideration the settled law of the Supreme Court passed in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690 and Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

14. Let the applicant- Vinod Kumar, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

sentences.text: (ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C./351 B.N.S.S.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
15. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

16. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
